assetRisk.scenario: Fiscal measurement dispute or misallocation arbitration
assetRisk.source: ~450 major custody transfer stations across gas grid interconnects, gas plants, and downstream refinery/terminal receipt skids. Consequence (~₹8 Cr) covers multi-month retroactive true-up adjustments, expert determination, arbitration costs, and contractual imbalance penalties. High alpha and beta because custody dispute prevention is overwhelmingly an audit-trail, calibration-tracking, and calculation integrity problem.

rationale: P36 Measurement Engineer spans midstream gas transmission (55%) and downstream refining/distribution (45%). Headcount of 85 seats is sized across ~16,000 km of gas transmission grid (~40 seats in regional measurement bases) and downstream operations (~45 seats across 11 refineries and ~120 marketing installations). Asset Capital is strictly null because measurement engineers do not sit on the critical path of physical asset throughput (gas and liquids flow uninterrupted, and duty/standby meter skids prevent outages). Asset Risk models major fiscal custody disputes and misallocation arbitration across 450 fiscal metering stations at ₹8 Cr average consequence with alpha*beta held to 0.14 (avoided risk of ₹15.12 Cr/yr). Resource Recovery is null as the role operates downstream of the reservoir.
caveats: Dispute consequences can surge during high gas price volatility or winter demand peaks when shipper imbalances carry steep financial surcharges. Dual-stream metering configurations ensure zero physical critical-path deferment, reinforcing the zero asset capital basis.
